5) Prompt template governance - versioning, system-prompt lifecycle, prompt injection mitigations, and red-team cadence.

Alex - adding Rishi (SE) and Connor (Solutions) to scope the technical deep dive. See inline answers + quick SDK snippet below. I attached the more detailed prompt-governance doc (RC1).

Auth recommendations:
- Short-lived tokens via our token-exchange endpoint is the recommended pattern. You mint a short-lived token from your platform identity provider (OIDC) and exchange it for a Redwood session token. We support mTLS for Private deployments where you want certificate-based mutual auth.
- SDKs: we provide a helper that accepts either an API key, an mTLS cert, or an OIDC-exchanged session token.

SDK snippet (Python) - redwood-sdk-auth-sample.py (attached)
from redwood import RedwoodClient

# Option A: short-lived session token obtained via OIDC exchange
client = RedwoodClient(token="eyJhbGci...")
resp = client.generate("Summarize: {{ticket_text}}", max_tokens=150)
print(resp.text)

# Option B: mTLS (Private)
client = RedwoodClient(endpoint="https://private.acme.redwood.local", cert=("/path/to/cert.pem", "/path/to/key.pem"))
resp = client.generate("Action: extract_link", structured=True)

Routing & deployment notes:
- Hosted -> Dedicated migration is config-only: model alias and routing policy are updated in the Console; SDK calls still go to the same API endpoint but a customer-specific routing header is sent. We'll share a Migration Runbook in the deep-dive.

Prompt governance (summary):
- Version prompts as immutable artifacts (v1, v2, v2.1) stored in a prompt registry (we can integrate with your Git repo).
- Each prompt version gets an associated eval suite; we gate rollout with canary traffic and regression alerts (quality metrics on your eval prompts).
- Mitigations for prompt injection: input sanitization, explicit system prompt constraints, structured output enforcement (schema + tool-calling), and LLM-level red-team tests.

Rishi will follow up with embedding + reranker pattern and recommended refresh cadence.

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue Oct 12 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed Oct 13 11:00-11:30 PT. Which works for your infra/security folks?

Thanks -
Marissa

Hi all -

Couple of specific recommendations from the infra/ML perspective based on your use-case:

Embeddings + reranker pattern:
- Indexing: nightly batch embed of KB articles with incremental updates for changed docs. Use a sparse + dense hybrid retrieval (TF-IDF prefilter -> vector search) to keep recall high.
- Reranker: lightweight cross-encoder reranker (finetune on your evaluation set) that runs on top-K (k=50) results; this improves precision for short answers.
- Refresh cadence: nightly ingest, immediate embed for hot edits. Store embeddings in a managed vector DB (we provide connectors to Faiss/Pinecone/Weaviate).

Structured output & tool-calling:
- Use a strict JSON Schema for actions (e.g., {"action": "create_ticket", "fields": {...}}). Enforce schema validation server-side before executing tool calls.
- For deterministic tasks (e.g., create JIRA ticket), prefer a tool endpoint invoked by the server after schema validation - this reduces injection surface.

Prompt versioning & canaries:
- Store system & user prompt templates as versioned artifacts. Each change triggers an automated eval (unit test style) against a prompt set and production-like samples.
- Canary rollout: start at 1% traffic, monitor quality/regression alerts for 48 hrs, then ramp. Keep automatic rollback rules if metrics degrade >X%.

Prompt injection mitigations (practical):
- Escape/uninterpret free-text where possible; for structured outputs, never ask the model to return raw executable commands.
- Use model-level safety prompts and response parsing; validate against the schema and apply heuristics to catch unusual tokens/commands.
- Red teaming: run adversarial prompt lists weekly against a staging environment; record failure cases and add to blocked patterns. See attached "red-teaming-checklist.xlsx" for an initial cadence.

I can join the Oct 12 deep-dive and bring a short slide with architecture drawings and a migration runbook.
